summary: MaterialDNA documents {id, recipeVersion} as durable canonical content identity and forbids reusing a published pair for different content, but current shipped fixture tests only pinned IDs, revision numbers, validity and coherence. A valid same-revision fixture edit could therefore silently change established truth without failing the MaterialDNA suite. Independent review of PR #283 is the intended follow-up; production identity remains {id, recipeVersion} with no competing material identity framework.
evidence: Docs/MATERIAL_DNA_CONTRACT.md requires recipeVersion to increase whenever canonical material truth changes and forbids published {id, recipeVersion} reuse for different content.
Pre-change tests/materialdna_contract.luau checked production fixture IDs and recipeVersion == 1 but did not seal full fixture content.
PR #283 adds test-only deterministic full-content goldens for all three production fixtures plus an adversarial same-revision static-friction drift case.
